entities.summary:
Charles Colbert, Marquis of Croissy was a French statesman and diplomat. He played a key role in the early 18th-century politics of France, serving as a prominent figure in the ministry of King Louis XV. Colbert's diplomatic efforts helped to maintain France's influence in Europe during a time of growing tensions between European powers.

Born in 1643, Colbert rose to prominence in the French court after his marriage to Madame de Montespan, a cousin of the king. His involvement in the king's inner circle and his connections to powerful nobles and financiers made him a valuable asset to the French government.

Colbert's tenure as marquis was marked by his role in the Treaty of Ryswick, which ended the War of the Spanish Succession and established France's dominance in Europe. He also played a key part in the development of the French financial system, helping to create the Banque de France and establishing the country's first national bank.

Despite his significant contributions to French politics and finance, Colbert's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by his more famous contemporaries, such as Voltaire and Diderot. However, his impact on French history cannot be overstated, as he helped to establish France as a major player in European politics and finance during a time of great change and upheaval.

Charles Colbert, Marquis of Croissy, died on July 28, 1696, leaving behind a legacy that continues to be felt in French politics and finance to this day.
